editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the fair-share window split (28-araw na rolling time window para sa Premium vs. buong subscription period para sa Flex), the four "what happens at the limit" bullets, and the allocation-limit vs. usage-limit distinction with usage_allocation_seconds all land exactly as in the English, with no dropped caveat, inverted condition, or invented claim; the "hindi itinakda bilang limitasyon → maaaring gumamit ng higit sa nakalaan nitong oras" warning is intact. Two editorial slips: the frontmatter description writes "kung gaano karaming oras ang pinapayagan ng isang instance na gamitin", where the ang/ng markers make the instance the one granting permission instead of the one being permitted — the body gets the same idea right ("kung aling mga instance ang pinapayagang gamitin ang oras na iyon"), so it is an inconsistency with the correct form rather than a genuine falsehood. And "Maaari mong opsyonal na itakda ang time allocation" is a calque of "You can optionally set"; no Tagalog technical writer stacks "opsyonal na" as an adverb inside the maaari + verb frame. Register is correctly casual (mo/iyo, no po/opo) and the kept-English terms (instance, allocation, workload, job, queue, usage window) are used consistently.

examples.source: Set, view, and change how much time an instance is allowed to use.
examples.translation: Itakda, tingnan, at baguhin kung gaano karaming oras ang pinapayagan ng isang instance na gamitin.
examples.suggested: Itakda, tingnan, at baguhin kung gaano karaming oras ang pinapayagang gamitin ng isang instance.
examples.why: The ang/ng marking reverses the roles: as written, the instance is the one doing the allowing. Line 9 already uses the correct pattern ("aling mga instance ang pinapayagang gamitin ang oras na iyon"), so this is also an internal inconsistency.

examples.source: You can optionally set the time allocation as a limit for the instance.
examples.translation: Maaari mong opsyonal na itakda ang time allocation bilang isang limitasyon para sa instance.
examples.suggested: Opsyonal mong maitatakda ang time allocation bilang limitasyon para sa instance.
examples.why: "Maaari mong opsyonal na itakda" is a word-order calque of "You can optionally set"; Tagalog does not stack the optionality adverb inside the maaari + verb frame. Meaning survives, but it reads as MT rather than native technical prose.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the negation in "Hindi tulad ng mga patakaran ng IAM, ang context-based restrictions ay hindi nagtatalaga ng access" is correct, the role matrix (Administrator on Qiskit Runtime Service for rules; Editor *or* Administrator on CBR for network zones; Viewer can only add zones to a rule) matches the English exactly, and the Activity Tracker sentence keeps the "not Qiskit Runtime Service" contrast. Terminology is consistent (rules→"mga panuntunan", policies→"mga patakaran", network zones→"mga network zone") and register is correctly informal ("iyong na-configure", no po/opo). The one thing a native technical editor would change is the calqued ligature construction "mga kahilingang access" / "isang kahilingang access" for "access request(s)" (used twice in the opening two paragraphs) — the linker reads as "request that is access"; idiomatic Tagalog would be "kahilingan sa access" or simply "access request".

examples.source: based on the context of access requests / an access request comes from an allowed context
examples.translation: batay sa konteksto ng mga kahilingang access ... kung ang isang kahilingang access ay nagmumula sa isang pinahintulutang konteksto
examples.suggested: batay sa konteksto ng mga kahilingan sa access ... kung ang isang kahilingan sa access ay nagmumula sa isang pinahintulutang konteksto
examples.why: The -ng ligature makes 'access' read as a modifier of 'kahilingan' ('request that is access') rather than the object of the request; native technical Tagalog links it with 'sa' (or keeps 'access request' whole). Meaning is still recoverable, so this is stylistic, not misleading.

editor_note: No inversions, swapped quantities, hallucinations or dropped caveats — both Flex Plan parentheticals and the 28-day window details survive intact, and the register is correctly casual (no po/opo). The weakest spot is "fair(ness)", rendered two ways: line 15 correctly uses "para sa layunin ng pagiging patas", but line 21 turns "fairly distributes resources to each instance" into "pantay-pantay na ipinamamahagi", which reads as *equally* — the opposite emphasis of a proportional-to-allocation scheduler, though the very next paragraph's doubling example limits the damage; "patas na ipinamamahagi" would fix it. "Construct" is mis-rendered as "konstruksyon" (physical construction/building) in the Instance definition where "konstrukto" or keeping "construct" is meant, and two sentences are stiff English-order calques ("Sa lahat ng bagay na pantay-pantay" for "With all else being equal"; "Ang mga account administrator ay pagkatapos ay magpapasya"). Also "contracted under their plan" softens to "nakasaad" (stated) rather than "nakakontrata".

examples.source: The fair-share scheduler uses the instances' allocation and current usage to schedule workloads in a manner that fairly distributes resources to each instance.
examples.translation: ...para mag-iskedyul ng mga workload sa paraang pantay-pantay na ipinamamahagi ang mga resources sa bawat instance.
examples.suggested: ...sa paraang patas na ipinamamahagi ang mga resources sa bawat instance.
examples.why: "pantay-pantay" means equally/evenly, but fair-share distributes proportionally to each instance's allocation — the next paragraph's "twice the minutes, twice the workloads" example contradicts an equal split. It is also inconsistent with "pagiging patas" used for fairness in line 15.

examples.source: The base-level construct to which time is allocated from the overarching account to a set of QPUs
examples.translation: Ang pinakabatayang konstruksyon kung saan inilaan ang oras mula sa pangunahing account para sa isang grupo ng mga QPU
examples.suggested: Ang pinakabatayang konstrukto (construct) kung saan inilalaan ang oras mula sa pangkalahatang account para sa isang grupo ng mga QPU
examples.why: "konstruksyon" in Tagalog means physical construction/building work, not an abstract organizational construct; recognizable from context but not the word a native technical writer would pick.

examples.source: With all else being equal, an instance with twice the number of minutes can execute twice the number of workloads.
examples.translation: Sa lahat ng bagay na pantay-pantay, ang isang instance na may doble ang bilang ng minuto ay maaaring mag-execute ng doble ang bilang ng mga workload.
examples.suggested: Kung pareho ang lahat ng ibang salik, ang instance na may doble ang bilang ng minuto ay makakapag-execute ng doble ang dami ng workload.
examples.why: Word-for-word calque of the English absolute construction; "Sa lahat ng bagay na pantay-pantay" is not idiomatic Tagalog and reads as machine output.

examples.source: Account administrators then decide what portion of this allocation to assign to each instance.
examples.translation: Ang mga account administrator ay pagkatapos ay magpapasya kung anong bahagi ng allocation na ito ang itatalaga sa bawat instance.
examples.suggested: Ang mga account administrator naman ang magpapasya kung anong bahagi ng allocation na ito ang itatalaga sa bawat instance.
examples.why: The stranded "ay pagkatapos ay" mirrors English "then" placement and produces a double-ay construction no native technical writer would use.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the "customers are not responsible for disaster recovery planning or actions" negation, the "any paid plan" scope, the "no noticeable degradation during a zonal failure" claim and the two-region list all survive intact, and register stays casual (no po/opo). Two editorial slips: the file splits "high availability" between a half-translated "mataas na availability" (frontmatter title + description) and the untranslated "high availability" used everywhere in the body and in the "## Arkitektura ng high availability" heading — pick one and keep it. Also "Kung may HA instance node o zone na mabigo" is stiff, calqued-from-English conditional syntax; a native writer would front the verb ("Kung mabigo ang isang HA instance node o zone"). Neither would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Understanding high availability and disaster recovery for Qiskit Runtime
examples.translation: Pag-unawa sa mataas na availability at disaster recovery para sa Qiskit Runtime
examples.suggested: Pag-unawa sa high availability at disaster recovery para sa Qiskit Runtime
examples.why: The title/description render the term as "mataas na availability" while the body and the H2 heading keep "high availability (HA)" in English throughout. Within-file split of the same core term; the English form is the one the body establishes and abbreviates as HA, so it should win.

examples.source: If an HA instance node or zone fails, the service continues to run API requests through to the surviving HA instance nodes.
examples.translation: Kung may HA instance node o zone na mabigo, ang serbisyo ay patuloy na nagpapatakbo ng mga API request sa pamamagitan ng mga natitirang HA instance node.
examples.suggested: Kung mabigo ang isang HA instance node o zone, patuloy pa ring ipinapadaan ng serbisyo ang mga API request sa mga natitirang HA instance node.
examples.why: "Kung may ... na mabigo" is a calqued existential conditional a Tagalog technical writer would not use; verb-initial phrasing reads naturally. Meaning is unchanged, so this is style, not drift.

editor_note: No semantic drift and nothing hallucinated: the prerequisite ordering (Install Qiskit → Set up your IBM Cloud account), the `pip install qiskit-ibm-runtime` instruction, and the "periodically check the release notes / we recommend frequently updating" admonition all carry the same force as the English, and the informal register holds throughout (no po/opo). Two small word-choice slips a native technical editor would fix: "Install the Qiskit SDK from source" is rendered "I-install ang Qiskit SDK mula sa pinagmulan" — "pinagmulan" reads as "origin/where it came from", not source code, which Filipino devs keep as "source" (or "source code"); and "updating your requirements for qiskit-ibm-runtime" becomes "i-update ang iyong mga kinakailangan", a literal reading of "requirements" that loses the pip dependency-spec sense. Neither would mislead a learner about how to install the package.

examples.source: Install the Qiskit SDK from source
examples.translation: I-install ang Qiskit SDK mula sa pinagmulan
examples.suggested: I-install ang Qiskit SDK mula sa source (source code)
examples.why: "Pinagmulan" means origin/provenance in ordinary Tagalog; "from source" is a build-from-source-code idiom that Filipino developers keep in English. The calque makes the link target vaguer than the English, though not wrong enough to mislead.

examples.source: We recommend frequently updating your requirements for `qiskit-ibm-runtime`
examples.translation: Inirerekumenda naming madalas na i-update ang iyong mga kinakailangan para sa `qiskit-ibm-runtime`
examples.suggested: ...na madalas i-update ang iyong requirements (dependency spec) para sa `qiskit-ibm-runtime`
examples.why: Here "requirements" is the pip/requirements-file sense, a term the field keeps in English; "mga kinakailangan" reads as generic "things that are needed" and flattens the packaging meaning.

examples.source: Install the Qiskit Runtime client so you can run jobs on IBM quantum computers.
examples.translation: I-install ang Qiskit Runtime client para makapatakbo ng mga job sa mga IBM quantum computer.
examples.suggested: ...para makapagpatakbo ka ng mga job sa mga IBM quantum computer.
examples.why: Minor form slip: "makapatakbo" is the intransitive-flavored form; the causative "makapagpatakbo ng mga job" is what a native technical writer would use for running jobs. Colloquially tolerated, so noted rather than counted as a defect.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful — nothing here would mislead a learner: the three IDP connection options, the "might incur a cost" caveat on App ID ("maaaring magkaroon ng bayad"), and the dynamic-rules tip ("para hindi mo na kailangang manu-manong idagdag ang bawat gumagamit sa bawat grupo") all match the English exactly, and the informal register ("iyong", "mo") holds with no po/opo. Two small non-native touches a Tagalog technical editor would fix: "sa lahat ng IBM® produkto" keeps English adjective-before-noun order, where native Tagalog is "sa lahat ng produkto ng IBM"; and "Sumangguni sa paksa na [Enabling authentication...]" needs the linker fused ("sa paksang") and reads stiffly compared with a simple "Basahin ang paksang...". Terminology is consistent throughout (user → "gumagamit" everywhere; IDP, App ID, SSO, single sign-on correctly kept in English). Also cosmetic: the final bullet moves the sentence period inside the link text ("[App ID documentation.]") instead of after it.

examples.source: Federate your users to all IBM® products with IBMid
examples.translation: I-federate ang iyong mga gumagamit sa lahat ng IBM® produkto gamit ang IBMid
examples.suggested: I-federate ang iyong mga gumagamit sa lahat ng produkto ng IBM® gamit ang IBMid
examples.why: "IBM produkto" copies English adjective-noun order; Tagalog attaches the brand as a possessive phrase after the noun ("produkto ng IBM"). Grammatical but reads as machine output.

examples.source: Refer to the [Enabling authentication from an external identity provider] topic.
examples.translation: Sumangguni sa paksa na [Enabling authentication from an external identity provider].
examples.suggested: Basahin ang paksang [Enabling authentication from an external identity provider].
examples.why: The linker should fuse to the noun ("paksang", not "paksa na"), and "Sumangguni sa" is bookish for a docs recommendation list; "Basahin ang" is what a native technical writer would use.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — nothing here would mislead a learner. The tricky Estimator sentence is preserved correctly ("ang mas mababang precision ay karaniwang nangangailangan ng mas maraming shots at samakatuwid ay mas matagal na oras ng pagpapatakbo"), the NoiseLearner caveat about a stale noise model and the "only practical if there is no long delay between jobs" condition both survive intact, and kept-English domain terms (shots, QPU consumption, precision, noise model, error mitigation/suppression, session, batch) are consistent. Two editor-level nits: (1) "kung walang matagal na pagitan sa pagitan ng mga job" stutters — "pagitan sa pagitan" is a redundancy a native technical writer would rewrite as "kung walang mahabang antala sa pagitan ng mga job"; (2) the translation adds bold emphasis absent from the English to the first three bullet leads and not the fourth, and in the third the bold closes mid-clause ("**...error suppression at error mitigation**, dahil..."), so the list is visually inconsistent with itself. Register is correctly casual — no po/opo anywhere.

examples.source: so this is only practical if there is no long delay between jobs (for example, within a session).
examples.translation: kaya praktikal lang ito kung walang matagal na pagitan sa pagitan ng mga job (halimbawa, sa loob ng isang session).
examples.suggested: kaya praktikal lang ito kung walang mahabang antala sa pagitan ng mga job (halimbawa, sa loob ng isang session).
examples.why: "pagitan sa pagitan" repeats the same root back-to-back — a stutter no native technical writer would leave; "antala" (delay) is the natural word for the first slot and keeps "sa pagitan ng" for "between".

examples.source: - Run only as many shots as you need: ... - Set limits on execution time: ... - Use only the necessary settings ... - If you are running multiple jobs ...
examples.translation: - **Magpatakbo lang ng kasing dami ng shots na kailangan mo:** ... - **Magtakda ng limitasyon sa oras ng pagpapatakbo:** ... - **Gamitin lang ang mga kinakailangang setting para sa error suppression at error mitigation**, dahil ... - Kung nagpapatakbo ka ng maraming job ...
examples.suggested: Either drop the bold from all four bullets to match the English, or apply it uniformly and close it at the colon (e.g. **Gamitin lang ang mga kinakailangang setting para sa error suppression at error mitigation:** dahil ...).
examples.why: Emphasis was invented in translation and applied to three of four bullets, and in the third it runs past the natural break into a mid-sentence comma, so the list reads unevenly compared with the source's flat parallel bullets.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim in the three source paragraphs (2016 start, "most popular quantum framework", "thanks in part to its vibrant community", the pull-requests-to-Slack range of contributions) survives intact, register is informal with no po/opo, and English domain nouns (quantum computing, framework, ecosystem, pull requests) are kept consistently. What a native editor would change is wording: "mapagkomang grupo" (line 16) is not a Tagalog word — "welcoming" should be "malugod na tumatanggap" / "mapagkupkop" — and bare "mahilig" for "enthusiasts" reads as a dangling adjective, needing "mga mahihilig sa quantum". The opening sentence (line 13) stacks "sa pamamagitan ng" twice in one clause, and line 17 calques "By making this ... open and accessible" as "Sa pamamagitan ng paggawa ng ... na bukas at accessible" instead of the natural "Sa pagbubukas at pagpapa-accessible ng teknolohiyang ito". All stylistic; nothing here would mislead a learner.

examples.source: The Qiskit community is a dynamic and welcoming group of developers, scientists, and enthusiasts
examples.translation: Ang komunidad ng Qiskit ay isang masigla at mapagkomang grupo ng mga developer, siyentipiko, at mahilig
examples.suggested: Ang komunidad ng Qiskit ay masigla at malugod na tumatanggap na grupo ng mga developer, siyentipiko, at mga mahihilig sa quantum
examples.why: "mapagkoma" is not an existing Tagalog word (looks like a garbled coinage for "welcoming"), and bare "mahilig" is an adjective left without a head noun, so "enthusiasts" reads incomplete.

examples.source: by making quantum computing resources accessible to everyone via the cloud
examples.translation: sa pamamagitan ng pagbibigay ng access sa quantum computing resources sa lahat sa pamamagitan ng cloud
examples.suggested: sa pagbibigay ng access sa quantum computing resources para sa lahat sa pamamagitan ng cloud
examples.why: "sa pamamagitan ng" appears twice in the same clause; a native technical writer would drop the first one and keep the instrumental phrase only for "via the cloud".

examples.source: By making this transformative technology open and accessible, we accelerate innovation
examples.translation: Sa pamamagitan ng paggawa ng transformative na teknolohiyang ito na bukas at accessible, pinapabilis natin ang inobasyon
examples.suggested: Sa pagbubukas at pagpapa-accessible ng mapagbagong teknolohiyang ito, pinabibilis natin ang inobasyon
examples.why: Calqued "by making X open and accessible" produces the stiff "paggawa ng ... na bukas"; Tagalog prefers a nominalized verb pair, and "transformative" could take a real Tagalog adjective here since it is prose, not a kept term.

editor_note: Short migration-index page, faithful throughout: "stability guarantees and performance improvements" → "mga bagong garantiya sa katatagan at mga pagpapabuti sa performance", and the breaking-change warning "hindi ito compatible sa lahat ng nakaraang bersyon ng Qiskit" reads with total-negation scope, matching the English "does break compatibility with all previous versions"; register is casual (iyong, no po/opo) and the three link labels track their targets exactly.

Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no dropped caveats, and no invented claims; the two template types (template implementation vs. base template), the AQC-Tensor/SQD addon pairings, and the "two templates: circuit function / application function" count all match the English exactly, and register stays casual (iyong/mo, no po/opo). Two wording slips a native technical editor would still change: "The repository is exposed as a GitHub template" is rendered "Ang repository ay inilalantad bilang isang GitHub template" — "inilalantad" carries the sense of exposing/revealing something concealed, not "made available as", so a native writer would use "nakalathala/ibinibigay bilang" or "ginawang GitHub template"; and "build from scratch" becomes the tautological "magsimula sa simula" instead of the idiomatic "magsimula mula sa wala" / "magsimula sa umpisa". Both are stylistic calques that do not mislead a learner. Domain terms (Hamiltonian simulation, electronic structure, implicit solvent model, classical compute, workflow, addon) are kept in English consistently, which is the right convention for this file.

examples.source: The repository is exposed as a GitHub template so that the CI/CD implementation can be easily extended.
examples.translation: Ang repository ay inilalantad bilang isang GitHub template para madaling mapalawak ang CI/CD implementation.
examples.suggested: Ang repository ay ibinibigay bilang isang GitHub template para madaling mapalawak ang CI/CD implementation.
examples.why: "Inilalantad" means to expose/reveal something hidden (often with a negative connotation); here "exposed" simply means "made available as". Calqued sense, not a meaning error.

examples.source: ...reuse in your own research so that you don't have to build from scratch.
examples.translation: ...gamitin muli sa iyong sariling research nang hindi na kailangang magsimula sa simula.
examples.suggested: ...gamitin muli sa iyong sariling research nang hindi na kailangang magsimula mula sa wala.
examples.why: "Magsimula sa simula" is a tautology in Tagalog; the idiomatic rendering of "from scratch" is "mula sa wala" (or "sa umpisa").

examples.source: They are designed to help you kickstart the development process...
examples.translation: Idinisenyo ang mga ito para tulungan kang simulan ang proseso ng development...
examples.suggested: Idinisenyo ang mga ito para mapabilis mo ang pagsisimula ng proseso ng development...
examples.why: "Kickstart" implies giving the process a fast start, not merely starting it; the emphasis is slightly flattened. Defensible as-is, noted only for completeness.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination anywhere: the three-year retention clause, the "(undeleted)" qualifier ("ang iyong data (na hindi nabura)"), the Manager-role condition, and "encrypted at rest" → "ine-encrypt habang nakaimbak" are all faithful, and the register is correctly informal (mo/iyong, no po/opo). What a native technical editor would change is grammar and stiffness: line 17 opens "Ang pagbura ng isang service instance ay aalisin ang lahat ng content…", which mismatches the ang-topic with a transitive -in verb (a calque of English "Deleting X removes Y"); it should be "Inaalis ng pagbura ng service instance ang lahat ng content…". Line 13's "random na nabuong key" is a word-order calque of "randomly generated key" and reads mechanically. Line 9 also drops the English emphasis "exactly" from "know exactly what data is stored" ("malaman kung anong data ang nakaimbak") — a lost qualifier, not a meaning change. Terminology (data, instance, job, encrypt, role) is consistent throughout; only the retain family varies stylistically (pagpapanatili / Itatago / pinananatili), which is acceptable Tagalog variation.

examples.source: Deleting a service instance removes all of the content associated with that instance, such as your jobs, results, parameters, and programs.
examples.translation: Ang pagbura ng isang service instance ay aalisin ang lahat ng content na nauugnay sa instance na iyon, tulad ng iyong mga job, resulta, parameter, at programa.
examples.suggested: Inaalis ng pagbura ng service instance ang lahat ng content na nauugnay sa instance na iyon, tulad ng iyong mga job, resulta, parameter, at programa.
examples.why: "Ang pagbura ... ay aalisin ang lahat" puts an ang-marked topic in front of a transitive -in verb that already takes "ang lahat" as its patient — ungrammatical, and a direct calque of the English "Doing X removes Y" frame. Meaning is still recoverable, so it does not mislead.

examples.source: The data that you store in IBM Cloud is encrypted at rest by using a randomly generated key.
examples.translation: Ang data na iniimbak mo sa IBM Cloud ay ine-encrypt habang nakaimbak gamit ang isang random na nabuong key.
examples.suggested: ... ay ine-encrypt habang nakaimbak gamit ang key na random na binuo.
examples.why: "random na nabuong key" copies English adjective order; Tagalog stacks the modifier after the head noun here. "habang nakaimbak" for "at rest" is a good, correct choice and should be kept.

examples.source: it is important to know exactly what data is stored and encrypted
examples.translation: mahalagang malaman kung anong data ang nakaimbak at ine-encrypt
examples.suggested: mahalagang malaman nang eksakto kung anong data ang nakaimbak at ine-encrypt
examples.why: The emphasis carried by "exactly" is dropped. The claim is not inverted or altered, so this is a lost qualifier rather than misleading content.

editor_note: No semantic drift anywhere: the 20-question count, the "hindi bababa sa 16" pass threshold, the two-attempt temporary lock ("pansamantalang mala-lock"), the maintenance notice, and the entire Credly/privacy paragraph (US-based third-party processor, name/email/badge shared, global subsidiary sharing) all match the English exactly, with no dropped caveat and nothing invented. Two style-level slips remain: the friendly survey paragraph uses stiff "ay"-inversion passive ("Ang iyong feedback ay gagamitin para mapahusay...") where the English is chatty and a native writer would use the active "Gagamitin namin ang iyong feedback...", and "passing score" is calqued as "pumapasang puntos" (twice), which reads as machine-literal — a Tagalog technical writer would say "pasadong marka" or simply keep "passing score". Register is otherwise correctly casual ("Binabati kita", "i-click ang button sa ibaba"), with no po/opo. Neither issue could mislead a learner.

examples.source: Your feedback will be used to enhance our content offering and user experience.
examples.translation: Ang iyong feedback ay gagamitin para mapahusay ang aming mga nilalaman at karanasan ng gumagamit.
examples.suggested: Gagamitin namin ang iyong feedback para mapahusay ang aming nilalaman at ang user experience.
examples.why: The 'ay'-inversion passive is a calque of the English passive and reads stiff in a paragraph the source keeps conversational; the active voice with 'namin' is what a native technical writer would use here.

examples.source: Upon receiving a passing score... If you don't receive a passing score in two attempts
examples.translation: Sa pagtanggap ng pumapasang puntos... Kung hindi ka makakakuha ng pumapasang puntos sa dalawang pagtatangka
examples.suggested: Kapag nakapasa ka... Kung hindi ka makapasa sa dalawang pagtatangka
examples.why: 'Pumapasang puntos' is a word-for-word rendering of 'passing score' that no Tagalog speaker would say; the idiomatic construction uses the verb 'makapasa'. Consistent within the file, so recognizable, but audibly machine-translated.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the *no-cloning theorem* / "kawalan ng posibilidad na perpektong makilala ang mga hindi orthogonal na quantum state" sentence tracks the English exactly, and domain terms (quantum circuit, inner products, orthogonality/orthonormality, projective measurements) are correctly kept in English and used consistently. Two things a native technical editor would still fix. First, a real grammatical slip in the opening paragraph: "maaari kang buksan ang [YouTube video]" mixes actor-focus "ka" with the object-focus verb "buksan" — it must be "maaari mong buksan ang YouTube video". Second, "we'll derive fundamental limitations" is flattened to "malalaman natin ang mga pundamental na limitasyon" ("we'll learn/know"), losing the pedagogical promise that the limits are *derived* from the concepts just introduced; "ilalahad/ihahango natin" would keep the emphasis. Register is correctly casual with no po/opo.

examples.source: Alternatively, you can open the [YouTube video] for this lesson in a separate window.
examples.translation: Bilang alternatibo, maaari kang buksan ang [YouTube video] para sa araling ito sa isang hiwalay na window.
examples.suggested: Bilang alternatibo, maaari mong buksan ang [YouTube video] para sa araling ito sa isang hiwalay na window.
examples.why: Focus/pronoun mismatch: the object-focus verb 'buksan' requires the genitive actor 'mo', not the nominative 'ka'. A native writer would never produce 'maaari kang buksan ang...'.

examples.source: Through these concepts, we'll derive fundamental limitations on quantum information...
examples.translation: Sa pamamagitan ng mga konseptong ito, malalaman natin ang mga pundamental na limitasyon sa quantum information...
examples.suggested: Sa pamamagitan ng mga konseptong ito, ihahango natin ang mga pundamental na limitasyon sa quantum information...
examples.why: 'derive' becomes 'malalaman' ('will come to know'), which softens the lesson's promise that these limits are formally derived from the inner-product/orthogonality machinery just introduced, not merely stated for the reader to absorb.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the framework sentence ("paglalarawan ng mga quantum state bilang mga vector", "mga operasyon ... na inilalarawan ng mga unitary matrix") tracks the English exactly, and the informal register holds with no po/opo. Three things a native technical editor would still change: "measurements" is rendered as "mga sukat" (= sizes/dimensions) where the domain term is "mga pagsukat" (the act of measuring); "considered in isolation" becomes "isinasaalang-alang nang mag-isa" ("alone/by itself") instead of "nang hiwalay / sa paghihiwalay"; and the future "we'll expand our view" is rendered with the hortative "palawakin natin" rather than the future "papalawakin natin". Also "mga complex number na entries" leaves "entries" as a bare unmarked English plural — a calqued construction a Tagalog writer would recast as "mga entry na complex number". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: measurements that allow classical information to be extracted from quantum states
examples.translation: mga sukat na nagpapahintulot na makuha ang klasikal na impormasyon mula sa mga quantum state
examples.suggested: mga pagsukat na nagpapahintulot na makuha ang klasikal na impormasyon mula sa mga quantum state
examples.why: "sukat" in Tagalog is a size/dimension; the quantum-information term for the act of measurement is "pagsukat". Recognizable in context, so minor, but it is the wrong nominalization for a core domain term.

examples.source: a *single system* is considered in isolation
examples.translation: ang isang *single system* ay isinasaalang-alang nang mag-isa
examples.suggested: ang isang *single system* ay sinusuri nang hiwalay
examples.why: "nang mag-isa" means "alone / by oneself" and reads oddly applied to a system; "in isolation" here means examined separately from others, which Tagalog expresses as "nang hiwalay". Also "isinasaalang-alang" (= taken into account) is a stiff literal fit for "considered" in the sense of "studied".

examples.source: In the next lesson, we'll expand our view to *multiple systems,*
examples.translation: Sa susunod na aralin, palawakin natin ang ating pananaw sa *multiple systems,*
examples.suggested: Sa susunod na aralin, papalawakin natin ang ating pananaw sa *multiple systems,*
examples.why: "palawakin natin" is the hortative/imperative form ("let's expand"); the English is a plain future statement of what the course will do, which takes the contemplative "papalawakin natin".

examples.source: quantum states as vectors with complex number entries
examples.translation: mga quantum state bilang mga vector na may mga complex number na entries
examples.suggested: mga quantum state bilang mga vector na ang mga entry ay complex number
examples.why: "mga ... na entries" double-marks plurality (Tagalog "mga" plus the English -s) and stacks two English nouns in a calqued English word order; a native technical writer would restructure rather than transliterate the noun pile.

editor_note: No semantic drift and nothing hallucinated: every claim in the four body paragraphs tracks the English, the "9-qubit Shor code" / "discretization of errors" italics survive, and the pessimism-then-optimism arc ("sa huli ay gagawing imposible" → "optimistiko … magiging katotohanan balang araw") is preserved intact. What a native technical editor would change is word choice: "very significant challenges" became "napakahalagang hamon" (= very *valuable/important* challenges, not substantial/major — "napakalaki/napakabigat na hamon" is the intended sense); "at the same time" became "sa kabilang banda" (= on the other hand), which keeps the contrast but drops the simultaneity that actually generates the tension the next sentence names; and "very precise control" became "napakasertong kontrol", an odd coinage where "napakatumpak na kontrol" is the standard rendering. Smaller slips: "measurements" rendered as "mga sukat" (reads as measures/dimensions rather than the act of measuring — "pagsusukat" is the domain term), "foundational concept" as the ungrammatical "pundasyon na konsepto", and a second-person mismatch in the video section where "tinuturuan kayo ni John Watrous" (plural/formal) is immediately followed by "maaari mong buksan" (informal singular). None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: There are, however, very significant challenges that must be overcome
examples.translation: Gayunpaman, may mga napakahalagang hamon na kailangang malampasan
examples.suggested: Gayunpaman, may mga napakalaking hamon na kailangang malampasan
examples.why: "Significant" here means substantial/major, not valuable. "Napakahalaga" means "very important/precious", which reframes obstacles as assets. Not misleading enough to teach a false concept, but a native writer would use "napakalaki" or "napakabigat".

examples.source: But, at the same time, quantum computers must provide very precise control over this quantum information
examples.translation: Ngunit, sa kabilang banda, kailangang magbigay ang mga quantum computer ng napakasertong kontrol sa quantum information na ito
examples.suggested: Ngunit, sa parehong pagkakataon, kailangang magbigay ang mga quantum computer ng napakatumpak na kontrol sa quantum information na ito
examples.why: "Sa kabilang banda" = "on the other hand", which loses the simultaneity that is the whole source of the tension the following sentence names ("malinaw na may tensyon sa pagitan ng mga kinakailangang ito"). Also "napakasertong" (from siyerto = certain) is an unnatural coinage for "precise"; "napakatumpak" is the term already used for "accurate" two clauses later.

examples.source: the ability to perform measurements so that the results of the computation can be obtained
examples.translation: kakayahang magsagawa ng mga sukat para makuha ang mga resulta ng computation
examples.suggested: kakayahang magsagawa ng mga pagsusukat para makuha ang mga resulta ng computation
examples.why: "Mga sukat" reads as measures/dimensions (a size), not the quantum operation of measuring. "Pagsusukat" (or keeping "measurement") is the conventional domain rendering; the concept stays recognizable, so this is minor.

examples.source: John Watrous steps you through the content in this lesson … Alternatively, you can open the YouTube video
examples.translation: tinuturuan kayo ni John Watrous sa nilalaman ng araling ito … maaari mong buksan ang YouTube video
examples.suggested: tinuturuan ka ni John Watrous sa nilalaman ng araling ito … maaari mong buksan ang YouTube video
examples.why: Second person flips from plural/formal "kayo" to informal singular "mo" within two sentences. The file's convention is casual, so "ka" is the consistent choice.

examples.source: a foundational concept in quantum error correction known as the discretization of errors
examples.translation: isang pundasyon na konsepto sa quantum error correction na kilala bilang ang discretization of errors
examples.suggested: isang pundamental na konsepto sa quantum error correction na kilala bilang discretization of errors
examples.why: "Pundasyon na konsepto" is ungrammatical noun-stacking (a linker calqued off English adjective order); "pundamental/pangunahing konsepto" is what a Tagalog technical writer would write. The trailing "bilang ang" is likewise a stiff English-article calque.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful throughout — the exam mechanics survive exactly (20 tanong, "hindi bababa sa 16 para makapasa", "sa dalawang pagtatangka, pansamantalang mala-lock ang pagsusulit"), and nothing in the Credly/privacy notice is dropped, softened, or invented; register stays casual with no po/opo. What a native technical editor would still fix sits entirely in the final NOTICE paragraph, which reads as clause-by-clause English word order: "Ang mga empleyado ng IBM ay maaaring tingnan ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement dito" puts two competing ang-phrases in one clause with an object-focus verb (natural Tagalog is "Maaaring tingnan ng mga empleyado ng IBM ang..."), and "Ito ay pamamahalaan nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM" is a stiff ay-passive calque of "It will be handled...". Smaller nit: "mga layuning operational" leaves an unassimilated English adjective where "operasyonal" is the ordinary Tagalog form. None of these change meaning — they are polish, not drift.

examples.source: IBM employees can view the IBM Internal Privacy Statement here.
examples.translation: Ang mga empleyado ng IBM ay maaaring tingnan ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement dito.
examples.suggested: Maaaring tingnan ng mga empleyado ng IBM ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement dito.
examples.why: Object-focus verb 'tingnan' with the actor marked by 'ang' creates a focus mismatch and two competing ang-phrases; a native writer marks the actor with 'ng' and fronts the verb.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Ito ay pamamahalaan nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.suggested: Pangangasiwaan ito nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.why: The 'Ito ay + verb' pattern is a direct calque of the English passive and the aspect form 'pamamahalaan' is unmarked; the standard Tagalog contemplative 'Pangangasiwaan ito...' reads naturally.

examples.source: for program reporting and operational purposes
examples.translation: para sa pag-uulat ng programa at mga layuning operational
examples.suggested: para sa pag-uulat ng programa at mga layuning operasyonal
examples.why: 'operational' is left as a raw English adjective inside an otherwise Tagalog noun phrase; 'operasyonal' is the established borrowing and matches the surrounding assimilated vocabulary.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no dropped caveats, and the technical content (CSS codes named for Calderbank/Shor/Steane, the toric code as an infinite family "isa para sa bawat positibong integer na mas malaki sa isa", surface/color codes) matches the source exactly. What a native technical editor would fix is surface craft: a garbled non-word "kayun" in para. 1 where "kaysa roon" belongs ("mas maraming error pa kayun"); the relative clause "ang mga unang natuklasan nito" which reverses agent and patient (reads as "the first things it discovered" instead of "who first discovered them" — should be "na siyang mga unang nakatuklas nito"), plus "pinangalan kay" for three people where "kina" is required; the calqued "Pinapayagan ng CSS code construction ang isa na kumuha" mirroring English "allows one to", with a verb-aspect mismatch in the coordinated "pagsasamahin" (should be "pagsamahin"); a missing linker in "isang pangunahin (at tunay na magandang) halimbawa"; and a second-person register split in the video paragraph, "iginagabay kayo ni John Watrous" against "maaari mong buksan" one clause later. None of these would teach a learner anything false.

examples.source: we're going to need to be able to tolerate a lot more errors than that
examples.translation: kailangan nating kayanin ang mas maraming error pa kayun
examples.suggested: kailangan nating kayanin ang mas marami pang error kaysa roon
examples.why: "kayun" is not a Tagalog word — it is a corrupted rendering of "kaysa roon"/"kaysa doon". The comparison target of "than that" is left dangling, so the sentence trips the reader even though the intent survives.

examples.source: named for Robert Calderbank, Peter Shor, and Andrew Steane, who first discovered them
examples.translation: na pinangalan kay Robert Calderbank, Peter Shor, at Andrew Steane, ang mga unang natuklasan nito
examples.suggested: na ipinangalan kina Robert Calderbank, Peter Shor, at Andrew Steane, na siyang mga unang nakatuklas nito
examples.why: "ang mga unang natuklasan nito" uses the object-focus form, so it literally reads "the first things discovered by it" — agent and patient are swapped. Also "kay" must be plural "kina" before three names.

examples.source: The CSS code construction allows one to take certain pairs of classical error correcting codes and combine them into a single quantum error correcting code.
examples.translation: Pinapayagan ng CSS code construction ang isa na kumuha ng ilang tiyak na *pares* ... at pagsasamahin ang mga ito sa iisang quantum error correcting code.
examples.suggested: Sa pamamagitan ng CSS code construction, maaaring kumuha ng ilang tiyak na *pares* ng classical error correcting codes at pagsamahin ang mga ito sa iisang quantum error correcting code.
examples.why: "ang isa" is a word-for-word calque of the impersonal English "one"; no Tagalog technical writer uses it. "pagsasamahin" (contemplative) also fails to agree with the infinitive "kumuha" it is coordinated with — should be "pagsamahin".

examples.source: John Watrous steps you through the content in this lesson
examples.translation: iginagabay kayo ni John Watrous sa nilalaman ng araling ito
examples.suggested: gagabayan ka ni John Watrous sa nilalaman ng araling ito
examples.why: "kayo" is the formal/plural second person, but the very next clause uses the casual singular "maaari mong buksan". The file mixes the two registers within one paragraph; the casual "ka/mo" convention should hold.

examples.source: This is a fundamental (and truly beautiful) example
examples.translation: Ito ay isang pangunahin (at tunay na magandang) halimbawa
examples.suggested: Ito ay isang pangunahing (at tunay na magandang) halimbawa
examples.why: Missing the linker -ng on "pangunahin" before the noun; the parallel adjective in the same parenthesis correctly carries it ("magandang"), which makes the omission stand out.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every clause of the four-sentence opening and the lesson-outline paragraph maps faithfully to the English, including the "Hindi lahat ng quantum error correcting code ay stabilizer code, ngunit marami ang ganoon" negation and the "Magbibigay ito ng pundasyon at magdadala sa atin" rendering of "will both inform and lead into", which is genuinely well-written Tagalog. Three editorial slips remain. (1) "measurements of qubits" is rendered "mga sukat ng qubits" — "sukat" reads as measurement-as-size/dimension; the domain sense (the act of measuring, contrasted with "operasyon sa qubits" in the same sentence) needs "pagsukat sa qubits". (2) "real-world quantum devices" becomes the doubled "mga tunay na quantum device sa totoong mundo" — same idea said twice; one of the two should go. (3) Second person is inconsistent within the file: the video paragraph uses plural/formal "ginagabayan kayo ni John Watrous" while the very next sentence uses casual singular "maaari kang magbukas".

examples.source: which can represent not only operations on qubits, but also measurements of qubits
examples.translation: na kayang kumatawan hindi lamang sa mga operasyon sa qubits, kundi pati na rin sa mga sukat ng qubits
examples.suggested: ...kundi pati na rin sa pagsukat sa mga qubit
examples.why: "sukat" carries the everyday sense of size/dimension; the sentence is contrasting an operation with the act of measuring, so "pagsukat" is the conventional domain rendering. Recognizable but imperfect — it does not teach a false concept.

examples.source: including codes that seem likely to be well-suited to real-world quantum devices
examples.translation: kabilang ang mga code na tila angkop para sa mga tunay na quantum device sa totoong mundo
examples.suggested: kabilang ang mga code na tila angkop para sa mga tunay na quantum device
examples.why: "tunay na ... sa totoong mundo" translates "real-world" twice; a native technical writer would keep only one.

examples.source: John Watrous steps you through the content in this lesson
examples.translation: ginagabayan kayo ni John Watrous sa nilalaman ng araling ito
examples.suggested: ginagabayan ka ni John Watrous sa nilalaman ng araling ito
examples.why: "kayo" is the plural/deferential you, while the next sentence in the same paragraph uses casual singular "maaari kang magbukas" — an inconsistent address within one paragraph and a slip from the file's informal convention.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the load-bearing facts survive intact: "20 tanong … kailangan mong sagutin nang tama ang hindi bababa sa 16 para makapasa" matches the 20/16 threshold, and "Kung hindi ka makapasa sa dalawang pagtatangka, pansamantalang ma-lo-lock ang pagsusulit" preserves the two-attempt lockout condition without inversion. No hallucinated claims, no dropped caveats; the Credly/privacy notice is complete (subsidiaries, third parties, global sharing all present). Two things a native technical editor would still change: "Ito ay hahawakan nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM" uses hahawakan (literally "will be grasped/held") for "handled", a literal calque where pangangasiwaan / pakikitunguhan is the idiomatic verb; and the notice paragraphs stack English-style "ay"-passives ("Ang iyong feedback ay gagamitin", "ang iyong badge ay awtomatikong ipapadala", "Ang iyong personal na impormasyon ay ginagamit") where a Tagalog writer would front the verb (Gagamitin ang iyong feedback…), which makes the prose read as translated rather than written. Neither misleads.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Ito ay hahawakan nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.suggested: Pangangasiwaan ito nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.why: "hahawakan" is the physical sense of "hold/grasp"; for data "handled" the idiomatic verb is pangangasiwaan (or pakikitunguhan). Recognizable in context, so not misleading, but a literal-word choice a native editor would replace.

examples.source: Your feedback will be used to enhance our content offering... / your badge will automatically be sent... / Your personal information is used to issue your badge
examples.translation: Ang iyong feedback ay gagamitin... / ang iyong badge ay awtomatikong ipapadala... / Ang iyong personal na impormasyon ay ginagamit...
examples.suggested: Gagamitin ang iyong feedback... / awtomatikong ipapadala ang iyong badge... / Ginagamit ang iyong personal na impormasyon...
examples.why: Three consecutive "ay"-inverted passives mirroring English subject-first word order. Grammatical, but the stacked pattern is the clearest tell of translationese; verb-initial phrasing is what a Tagalog technical writer would produce.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful — the $O(\sqrt{N})$ worst-case lower bound, the "known even before Grover's algorithm was discovered" ordering, the quadratic success-probability boost of amplitude amplification, and the hedged closing ("maaaring hindi humantong ... sa malapit na hinaharap") all match the English with no inverted negation, swapped quantity or dropped caveat, and terminology (query model, lower bound, square-root speed-up, subroutine, amplitude amplification) is kept in English consistently. What a native technical editor would change is all translationese: "Sa wakas" is used for discourse "Finally," but means "at last, after a long wait" — it should be "Panghuli"; "makakasumpong ng maraming aplikasyon" is a word-for-word calque of "finds many applications" using an archaic/literary verb no technical writer would use; "nang kasabay ng ibang algorithm" renders "in conjunction with" as "simultaneously with" rather than "in combination with"; and "napatunayan nang mahigpit" calques "proved rigorously" with the literal sense of *mahigpit* (tight/strict). None of these would give a learner a false belief about the algorithm, so this is stylistic cleanup, not a correctness fix.

examples.source: Finally, the technique used in Grover's algorithm, where two reflections are composed and iterated to rotate a quantum state vector, can be generalized.
examples.translation: Sa wakas, ang teknik na ginamit sa Grover's algorithm, kung saan dalawang reflection ang pinagsama at inulit para mag-rotate ng quantum state vector, ay maaaring gawing mas pangkalahatan.
examples.suggested: Panghuli, ang teknik na ginamit sa Grover's algorithm, kung saan dalawang reflection ang pinagsama at inulit para mag-rotate ng quantum state vector, ay maaaring gawing mas pangkalahatan.
examples.why: 'Sa wakas' means 'at last / finally, after a long wait' — an emotional discourse marker. English 'Finally,' here is enumerative ('lastly'), which in Tagalog is 'Panghuli'. Classic MT slip a native writer would never make in expository prose.

examples.source: it is representative of a more general technique that finds many applications in quantum algorithms.
examples.translation: kinakatawan nito ang isang mas pangkalahatang teknik na makakasumpong ng maraming aplikasyon sa mga quantum algorithm.
examples.suggested: kinakatawan nito ang isang mas pangkalahatang teknik na may maraming aplikasyon sa mga quantum algorithm.
examples.why: 'makakasumpong' (from the literary/archaic *masumpungan*, 'to come upon') is a literal calque of the English idiom 'finds applications'. In Tagalog the verb reads biblical/archaic and is jarring in technical prose; the idiom does not transfer and should be flattened to 'may maraming aplikasyon'.

examples.source: sometimes it's possible to use Grover's algorithm in conjunction with another algorithm to get an improvement.
examples.translation: minsan posible na gamitin ang Grover's algorithm nang kasabay ng ibang algorithm para makakuha ng pagpapabuti.
examples.suggested: minsan posible na gamitin ang Grover's algorithm kasama ng ibang algorithm para makakuha ng pagpapabuti.
examples.why: 'kasabay' primarily means 'at the same time as / concurrently', which nudges the reader toward parallel execution rather than the intended 'in combination with'. 'kasama ng' or 'kaugnay ng' carries the compositional sense the English means.

examples.source: This is something that has been proved rigorously in multiple ways.
examples.translation: Ito ay isang bagay na napatunayan nang mahigpit sa maraming paraan.
examples.suggested: Ito ay isang bagay na masusing napatunayan sa maraming paraan.
examples.why: 'nang mahigpit' takes the literal sense of *mahigpit* (tight, strict, as in a strict rule or a tight grip) and attaches it to a proof; it does not idiomatically mean 'rigorously' in a mathematical sense. 'masusi' (thorough, meticulous) is the natural collocation with 'napatunayan'.

editor_note: Meaning is broadly faithful and no claim is inverted, but the asymptotic hedge "on the order of" is rendered two different ways in adjacent clauses of the same sentence: first as "katumbas ng *square root*" (= "equal to the square root", which drops the order-of hedge and states an exact equality) and then correctly as "hindi bababa sa antas ng *square*". A learner reading only the first clause could conclude Grover costs exactly sqrt(N) operations. Two emphasis flatteners: "staggering clock speeds" becomes just "nakamamanghang bilis" (clock speed dropped), and "still very much in its infancy" is softened to "bago pa rin" ("still new"), losing the English's deliberate contrast with mature classical computing. Register is correctly informal throughout (no po/opo); one stiff spot is "inagapayan ni John Watrous ang nilalaman" for "steps you through the content" — nonstandard form and wrong tense; a native writer would say "gagabayan ka ni John Watrous sa nilalaman."

examples.source: Grover's algorithm requires a number of operations on the order of the *square-root* of the number of operations required to solve unstructured search classically
examples.translation: ang Grover's algorithm ay nangangailangan ng bilang ng mga operasyon na katumbas ng *square root* ng bilang ng mga operasyong kailangan para malutas ang unstructured search sa klasikal na paraan
examples.suggested: ...na nasa antas ng *square root* ng bilang ng mga operasyong kailangan...
examples.why: "katumbas ng" means "equal to", turning an order-of-magnitude statement into an exact equality; the same phrase is correctly rendered "nasa antas ng" later in the very same sentence, so the file is also internally inconsistent on this hedge.

examples.source: is sure to be washed away by the staggering clock speeds of modern classical computers
examples.translation: ay tiyak na mawawala dahil sa nakamamanghang bilis ng mga modernong klasikal na computer
examples.suggested: ...dahil sa nakamamanghang clock speed ng mga modernong klasikal na computer
examples.why: "clock speeds" is the concrete hardware fact carrying the argument; flattening it to generic "bilis" weakens why the quadratic edge gets erased.

examples.source: While this technology is still very much in its infancy in comparison to classical computing
examples.translation: Bagaman ang teknolohiyang ito ay bago pa rin kumpara sa klasikal na computing
examples.suggested: Bagaman napakabata pa ng teknolohiyang ito kumpara sa klasikal na computing
examples.why: "very much in its infancy" is markedly stronger than "bago pa rin" ("still new"); the English intensifier sets up the concessive that follows.

examples.source: John Watrous steps you through the content in this lesson
examples.translation: inagapayan ni John Watrous ang nilalaman ng araling ito
examples.suggested: gagabayan ka ni John Watrous sa nilalaman ng araling ito
examples.why: "inagapayan" is a nonstandard form (and past tense where the English is present), and it drops the second-person "you" that makes the sentence read as instruction rather than narration.

examples.source: While the broad applicability of Grover's searching technique is compelling
examples.translation: Bagaman ang malawak na kakayahang magamit ng pamamaraan ng paghahanap ng Grover ay kapansin-pansin
examples.suggested: ...ay nakakahikayat / kapani-paniwala
examples.why: "kapansin-pansin" means merely "noticeable/striking"; "compelling" here means persuasive enough to be worth pursuing, so the rhetorical setup for the following caveat is slightly weakened.

editor_note: No semantic drift, no hallucination, and no dropped caveat — the course description, the exam/badge instructions, and the full Credly privacy notice all match the English claim for claim, and the informal register holds throughout (no po/opo). Two things a native technical editor would still change, both stylistic: "including" is calqued twice as "kasama ang" ("kasama kung ano ang magagawa natin..." and "para sa mga problemang kasama ang integer factorization at unstructured search"), which reads as machine-shaped English syntax where "tulad ng" / "gaya ng" is the idiomatic Tagalog; and the Credly paragraph's closing sentence "Ang mga empleyado ng IBM ay maaaring tingnan ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement dito" has a verb-focus mismatch — an ang-marked actor topic paired with the object-focus verb "tingnan" — which a native writer would recast as "Matitingnan ng mga empleyado ng IBM ang..." Neither would mislead a learner; core domain phrases (quantum query algorithm, integer factorization, unstructured search, quantum information) are kept in English consistently, which is the right convention here.

examples.source: then moves on to quantum algorithms for problems including integer factorization and unstructured search
examples.translation: pagkatapos ay lumipat sa mga quantum algorithm para sa mga problemang kasama ang integer factorization at unstructured search
examples.suggested: pagkatapos ay lumilipat sa mga quantum algorithm para sa mga problemang tulad ng integer factorization at unstructured search
examples.why: "kasama ang" is a literal calque of "including"; in Tagalog it reads as "accompanied by" rather than "such as", so the enumeration sounds machine-assembled. "tulad ng" is what a native technical writer uses. The same calque appears one sentence earlier ("kasama kung ano ang magagawa natin").

examples.source: IBM employees can view the IBM Internal Privacy Statement here.
examples.translation: Ang mga empleyado ng IBM ay maaaring tingnan ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement dito.
examples.suggested: Matitingnan ng mga empleyado ng IBM ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement dito.
examples.why: Focus mismatch: the actor is ang-marked as the topic while the verb "tingnan" is object-focus, and "ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement" is also ang-marked — two topics in one clause. Grammatically off, not just stiff; the actor should be ng-marked.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the Shor's-algorithm / quantum-Fourier-transform framing and the "implemented efficiently by a quantum circuit" claim all survive intact, and domain terms (phase estimation, quantum Fourier transform, integer factorization) are correctly kept in English. Three things a native technical editor would still fix. (1) Second person is inconsistent within one paragraph: "ginagabayan kayo ni John Watrous" uses the plural/polite kayo, then the next sentence switches to singular informal "maaari mong buksan" — the casual convention wants ka/mo in both. (2) "efficient" is rendered as "mahusay" ("isang mahusay na quantum algorithm", "ipatupad nang mahusay"), which reads as "excellent/skillful" rather than the complexity-theory sense; "episyente" or "mabisa" is the precise term, though the file is at least consistent so the learner is not misled. (3) Aspect wobbles inside the IBMVideo title — imperfective "sinusuri"/"isinasagawa" then completed "lumipat" for English's present-tense "moves on".

examples.source: In the following video, John Watrous steps you through the content in this lesson ... Alternatively, you can open the YouTube video
examples.translation: Sa sumusunod na video, ginagabayan kayo ni John Watrous sa nilalaman ng araling ito ... Bilang alternatibo, maaari mong buksan ang YouTube video
examples.suggested: Sa sumusunod na video, ginagabayan ka ni John Watrous sa nilalaman ng araling ito ... Bilang alternatibo, maaari mong buksan ang YouTube video
examples.why: kayo (plural/polite) and mo (singular informal) address the reader two different ways in adjacent sentences; the course register is casual, so ka/mo should be used consistently.

examples.source: an efficient quantum algorithm for the integer factorization problem ... how it can be implemented efficiently by a quantum circuit
examples.translation: isang mahusay na quantum algorithm para sa problema ng integer factorization ... kung paano ito maaaring ipatupad nang mahusay ng isang quantum circuit
examples.suggested: isang episyenteng quantum algorithm para sa problema ng integer factorization ... kung paano ito maaaring ipatupad nang episyente ng isang quantum circuit
examples.why: "Efficient" here is the technical complexity claim (polynomial-time), not praise. Mahusay reads as "excellent/skillful" and softens the point; episyente/mabisa carries the intended sense. Used consistently, so recognizable but imprecise.

examples.source: John Watrous reviews the phase estimation problem and steps through the phase estimation procedure. With this in hand, John moves on to Shor's algorithm.
examples.translation: sinusuri ni John Watrous ang problema ng phase estimation at isinasagawa ang pamamaraan ng phase estimation. Gamit ito, lumipat si John sa algorithm ni Shor.
examples.suggested: sinusuri ni John Watrous ang problema ng phase estimation at dinadaanan nang hakbang-hakbang ang pamamaraan ng phase estimation. Gamit ito, lilipat si John sa algorithm ni Shor.
examples.why: Aspect shifts mid-sentence from imperfective (sinusuri/isinasagawa) to completed (lumipat) where the English stays present tense; also "isinasagawa" (carries out) loses the walk-you-through-it sense of "steps through".

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no hallucinated claims; the argument of every paragraph (query model vs. explicit-input model, cost-as-scaling rather than wall-clock seconds, classical computation as quantum *subroutines*) survives intact, and the informal register holds with no po/opo. What a native technical editor would still fix is a cluster of calqued syntax and one malformed coinage: "nagsiskalang ang gastos" (line 25) is not a real Tagalog verb form for "scales" — "kung paano nag-i-scale/lumalaki ang gastos" is what a Filipino engineer would write. Twice the relative clause reverses agent and patient — "hardware na pinagpapatakbo ng mga ito" (line 24) and "instance ng problema na pinatatakbo nito" (line 25) literally say the algorithms run the hardware / run the instances, where the English says the reverse ("run ON"); the correct form is "pinagpapatakbuhan/pinatatakbuhan". Smaller slips: "nangyari ring lubhang may kaugnayan" is a word-for-word calque of "happen to be"; "sa lalong madaling panahon" idiomatically means ASAP rather than "any time soon"; "ang dekada ng pananaliksik" drops the plural of "decades"; and the heading sentence leaves "mga pundasyon ng quantum algorithmic" with a dangling adjective and no noun.

examples.source: how the cost of running an algorithm scales as the specific problem instances it's run on grow in size
examples.translation: kung paano nagsiskalang ang gastos ng pagpapatakbo ng isang algorithm habang lumalaki ang laki ng mga partikular na instance ng problema na pinatatakbo nito
examples.suggested: kung paano lumalaki (nag-i-scale) ang gastos ng pagpapatakbo ng isang algorithm habang lumalaki ang mga partikular na instance ng problemang pinatatakbuhan nito
examples.why: 'nagsiskalang' is a malformed verb coinage no Tagalog technical writer would produce; and 'pinatatakbo nito' reverses the roles — it says the algorithm runs the instances, whereas English says the algorithm is run ON them ('pinatatakbuhan'). Meaning is still recoverable, so this is stiffness plus a grammatical slip, not drift.

examples.source: as opposed to the ever-improving hardware on which they're run
examples.translation: kumpara sa patuloy na umuusbong na hardware na pinagpapatakbo ng mga ito
examples.suggested: kumpara sa patuloy na umuunlad na hardware na pinagpapatakbuhan ng mga ito
examples.why: Same reversed relative clause ('hardware that these run' instead of 'hardware they are run on'), and 'umuusbong' (emerging) is not 'ever-improving' — 'umuunlad' is the right verb.

examples.source: (and they also happen to be highly relevant to the lesson following this one)
examples.translation: (at nangyari ring lubhang may kaugnayan ang mga ito sa araling kasunod nito)
examples.suggested: (at nagkataon ding lubhang may kaugnayan ang mga ito sa susunod na aralin)
examples.why: 'nangyari ring' is a literal word-for-word calque of 'happen to be'; the idiomatic Tagalog for the incidental sense is 'nagkataon'. Grammatical but unmistakably translated rather than written.

examples.source: which seems extremely unlikely to happen any time soon, if ever … leveraging decades of research and development
examples.translation: na tila labis na hindi malamang mangyari sa lalong madaling panahon, kung meron man … ginagamit ang dekada ng pananaliksik at pag-unlad
examples.suggested: na tila napakaliit ng tsansang mangyari sa malapit na hinaharap, kung mangyari man … ginagamit ang ilang dekada ng pananaliksik at pag-unlad
examples.why: 'sa lalong madaling panahon' idiomatically means 'as soon as possible', not 'any time soon'; 'kung meron man' renders 'if ever' as 'if there is any'; and 'ang dekada' drops the plural of 'decades'. Each is a dropped/blunted qualifier rather than a reversal, so minor, but a native editor would fix all three.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the substantive claims all survive intact — "quantifiable advantages of quantum over classical computers" → "mga nasusukat na kalamangan ng quantum kumpara sa mga klasikal na computer", the "more robust and satisfying advantage" caveat and its "for reasons that will be explained when we get to it" hedge are both preserved, and terms (query model, petri dish, integer factorization, Deutsch-Jozsa) are kept in English consistently. What a native technical editor would still change is verb choice in three spots: "we'll formulate a simple algorithmic framework" is flattened to "mag-aaral tayo ng isang simpleng algorithmic framework" (we'll *study*, losing the sense that the lesson builds the model); "John Watrous steps you through the content" becomes "iginagabayan ni John Watrous ang mga nilalaman ng leksyong ito", which makes the *content* the thing being guided rather than the reader; and the video title renders "steps through some canonical examples" as "isinasabuhay ang ilang canonical na halimbawa" ("puts into practice / lives out"), which is not what stepping through an example means. Also "It's rigid" → "Ito ay mahigpit" reads as "strict" rather than inflexible. All four are stiffness/word-choice slips, none of them mislead; register stays casual throughout with no po/opo.

examples.source: we'll formulate a simple algorithmic framework — known as the *query model*
examples.translation: mag-aaral tayo ng isang simpleng algorithmic framework — kilala bilang ang *query model*
examples.suggested: bubuo tayo ng isang simpleng algorithmic framework — kilala bilang ang *query model*
examples.why: "Formulate" signals the lesson constructs the model from scratch; "mag-aaral" (we'll study) makes it sound like a pre-existing thing merely being read about, softening the framing of the whole course opener.

examples.source: John Watrous steps you through the content in this lesson on quantum query algorithms.
examples.translation: iginagabayan ni John Watrous ang mga nilalaman ng leksyong ito sa quantum query algorithms.
examples.suggested: gagabayan ka ni John Watrous sa mga nilalaman ng leksyong ito tungkol sa quantum query algorithms.
examples.why: The Tagalog makes "ang mga nilalaman" (the content) the thing being guided instead of the reader; the direct-address "you" of the English is dropped and the sentence reads as a calque a native writer would not produce.

examples.source: steps through some canonical examples from quantum computing
examples.translation: isinasabuhay ang ilang canonical na halimbawa mula sa quantum computing
examples.suggested: dinadaanan nang isa-isa ang ilang canonical na halimbawa mula sa quantum computing
examples.why: "Isinasabuhay" means "puts into practice / lives out" — a wrong sense for walking through a worked example step by step; the video description promises something different from what it delivers.

examples.source: It's rigid and unnatural in the sense that it doesn't accurately represent...
examples.translation: Ito ay mahigpit at hindi natural sa kahulugang hindi nito tumpak na kinakatawan...
examples.suggested: Ito ay matigas at hindi natural sa diwang hindi nito tumpak na kinakatawan...
examples.why: "Mahigpit" reads as "strict/tight" (as of a rule or a grip), not "inflexible", which is the sense of a rigid model; "sa kahulugang" is also a literal calque of "in the sense that" where "sa diwang" is the idiomatic choice.

editor_note: No semantic drift anywhere: the exam facts survive intact ("20 tanong", "hindi bababa sa 16 para makapasa", "sa dalawang pagtatangka, pansamantalang mala-lock ang pagsusulit"), and the Credly/privacy notice is faithful clause by clause. What a native editor would fix are grammar and translationese slips in the legal paragraph: "para tulungan sa pamamahala ng IBM Digital Badge program" uses the transitive "tulungan" with no object where "para tumulong sa pamamahala" is required; "para sa pag-uulat ng programa at mga layuning operasyon" leaves "operational" as the noun "operasyon" instead of "operasyonal"/"pang-operasyon"; and that same paragraph stacks three English-shaped "ay" passives in a row ("ang iyong personal na impormasyon ay ibabahagi", "ay ginagamit", "Ito ay pamamahalaan") where Tagalog would front the verb. Also "mala-lock" is a nonstandard reduplication (native Taglish future is "malo-lock"), and "badge na natanggap" renders "badge earned" as merely "received", losing the achievement sense. Register is correctly casual throughout — "Mangyaring" is polite-neutral, no po/opo.

examples.source: to assist in the administration of the IBM Digital Badge program
examples.translation: para tulungan sa pamamahala ng IBM Digital Badge program
examples.suggested: para tumulong sa pamamahala ng IBM Digital Badge program
examples.why: "tulungan" is the transitive/object-focus form and demands a direct object; with none present the clause is ungrammatical. The actor-focus "tumulong" is what a native writer uses for "assist in".

examples.source: for program reporting and operational purposes
examples.translation: para sa pag-uulat ng programa at mga layuning operasyon
examples.suggested: para sa pag-uulat ng programa at mga layuning operasyonal
examples.why: "operasyon" is the noun; modifying "layunin" needs the adjective "operasyonal" (or "pang-operasyon"). As written it reads as "purposes [of] operation" in a stilted, calqued way.

examples.source: Your personal information is used to issue your badge... IBM may share... It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Ang iyong personal na impormasyon ay ginagamit para maibigay ang iyong badge... Ito ay pamamahalaan sa paraang naaayon sa mga patakaran ng IBM sa privacy.
examples.suggested: Ginagamit ang iyong personal na impormasyon para maibigay ang iyong badge... Pamamahalaan ito nang naaayon sa mga gawi ng IBM sa privacy.
examples.why: Three consecutive "ay"-fronted passives mirror English word order rather than Tagalog's verb-initial default, giving the paragraph an unmistakable MT cadence. Separately, "practices" is flattened to "patakaran" (policies) rather than "gawi"/"mga kasanayan".

examples.source: the exam becomes temporarily locked
examples.translation: pansamantalang mala-lock ang pagsusulit
examples.suggested: pansamantalang malo-lock ang pagsusulit
examples.why: Taglish CV-reduplication copies the first consonant-vowel of the root, so "lock" gives "lo" (malo-lock), not "la". Meaning is clear, but the form is nonstandard.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the universal quantifier and its caveat ("*bawat* estado ρ ay may purification, basta't ... ang bahagi ng compound system na ini-trace out"), the "mas malaki ngunit mas simple" dilation gloss, and fidelity as "nagsusukat ng pagkakatulad" all match the English with no drift, softening, or invented claims; terminology (purification, fidelity, density matrix, compound system, pure state) is kept in English consistently with "estado" for the generic noun, and register stays informal. Three surface slips a native technical editor would fix: line 17 "Karaniwan at kapaki-pakinabang ang pag-isipan ang mga purification" double-marks with "ang" and is ungrammatical; line 19 coins "pagrestrikt" for "restricting" instead of an idiomatic "paghihigpit"/"paglilimita"; line 15 renders "large enough" as "malaki nang husto" ("greatly large") where sufficiency calls for "sapat na malaki". None of these would mislead a learner about the physics or the math — they are fluency/idiom repairs only.

examples.source: It's both common and useful to consider purifications of states when reasoning about them.
examples.translation: Karaniwan at kapaki-pakinabang ang pag-isipan ang mga purification ng mga estado kapag pinag-aaralan ang mga ito.
examples.suggested: Karaniwan at kapaki-pakinabang na isipin ang mga purification ng mga estado kapag pinag-aaralan ang mga ito.
examples.why: 'ang pag-isipan ang' double-marks the same clause with 'ang' — ungrammatical. The gerund either takes 'sa' ('ang pag-iisip sa mga purification') or the whole predicate becomes 'na isipin ang'. Meaning is unaffected, but no native technical writer would leave this.

examples.source: ...where something relatively complicated is obtained by restricting or reducing something larger yet simpler.
examples.translation: ...kung saan ang isang bagay na medyo kumplikado ay nakukuha sa pamamagitan ng pagrestrikt o pagbabawas ng isang mas malaki ngunit mas simpleng bagay.
examples.suggested: ...sa pamamagitan ng paghihigpit o pagbabawas ng isang mas malaki ngunit mas simpleng bagay.
examples.why: 'pagrestrikt' is an unassimilated English stem with no proper Tagalog affixation — it reads as raw borrowing. 'paghihigpit', 'paglilimita', or a hyphenated 'pagre-restrict' are all idiomatic. The 'mas malaki ngunit mas simple' half of the sentence is rendered correctly, so the dilation intuition survives.

examples.source: ...provided that the portion of the compound system that gets traced out is large enough.
examples.translation: ...basta't malaki nang husto ang bahagi ng compound system na ini-trace out.
examples.suggested: ...basta't sapat na malaki ang bahagi ng compound system na ini-trace out.
examples.why: 'nang husto' means 'thoroughly/to a great degree', not 'enough'. The sufficiency condition — which is the load-bearing caveat on the 'every state has a purification' claim — is still recoverable, but 'sapat na malaki' is the standard way to say 'large enough' and states the threshold rather than the magnitude.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, dropped caveats, or hallucinated claims; the "channel comes from information theory / terminology merely reflects historical motivation" paragraph and the discrete-time tooltip both track the English exactly, and the informal register holds with no po/opo. Three things a native technical editor would still change: "measurements" is rendered as "mga sukat" (line 15), which reads as "measures/dimensions" rather than the act of measuring — "mga pagsukat" is the conventional term, and this file will pair with the next lesson where measurement-as-channel is the whole topic; "equivalent mathematical characterizations" flattens to "katumbas na matematikong katangian" (line 25), where "katangian" = properties rather than characterizations, softening the point that the three representations each fully pin down what a channel is; and line 19 has a focus mismatch, "ang isang quantum channel ay maaaring tukuyin ang quantum state" (object-focus verb under an ang-topic), which a native writer would render "maaaring tukuyin ng quantum channel ang quantum state" or "maaaring tumukoy sa quantum state". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: We can also describe measurements as channels, which we'll do in the next lesson.
examples.translation: Maaari rin nating ilarawan ang mga sukat (measurements) bilang channels, na gagawin natin sa susunod na aralin.
examples.suggested: Maaari rin nating ilarawan ang mga pagsukat bilang channels, na gagawin natin sa susunod na aralin.
examples.why: "sukat" denotes a measure/size/dimension; the process sense needed here (a measurement as an operation on a state) is "pagsukat". The parenthetical English gloss rescues comprehension, so this is minor, but it is the wrong noun for a lesson whose sequel treats measurement as a channel.

examples.source: We'll see that, although these representations are different, they all offer equivalent mathematical characterizations of channels.
examples.translation: Makikita natin na, kahit magkaiba ang mga representasyong ito, lahat sila ay nag-aalok ng katumbas na matematikong katangian ng mga channel.
examples.suggested: ...lahat sila ay nagbibigay ng magkakatumbas na matematikang paglalarawan (characterization) ng mga channel.
examples.why: "katangian" means property/attribute, not characterization. The English claim is that each representation is a complete, mutually equivalent way of specifying a channel; "nag-aalok ng katumbas na katangian" downgrades that to the three merely sharing a property. Meaning is recoverable from context, so minor, but the pedagogical emphasis is flattened.

examples.source: In this context, a quantum channel could specify the quantum state that's received when a given quantum state is sent, perhaps through a quantum network of some sort.
examples.translation: Sa kontekstong ito, ang isang quantum channel ay maaaring tukuyin ang quantum state na natatanggap kapag ang isang ibinigay na quantum state ay ipinadala...
examples.suggested: Sa kontekstong ito, maaaring tukuyin ng isang quantum channel ang quantum state na natatanggap kapag may ipinadalang quantum state...
examples.why: Focus mismatch: "ay maaaring tukuyin ang X" puts an object-focus verb under an ang-marked actor topic, which a Tagalog technical writer would not produce; it is calqued from the English subject-verb-object order. The stacked passive "ang isang ibinigay na quantum state ay ipinadala" compounds the stiffness.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads: the exam mechanics are faithful (20 tanong, "hindi bababa sa 16 para makapasa", two-attempt lock, badge emailed to the IBM Training registration address) and the register is correctly casual with no po/opo. Three things a native technical editor would still change. (1) "Pagkatapos mabasa ang mga aralin at gawain sa kursong ito" flattens "After completing the reading and activities" into "after reading the lessons and activities" — you complete gawain, you don't read them; "Pagkatapos matapos ang mga babasahin at gawain" preserves it. (2) The Credly notice is calqued: "Ito ay hahawakan nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM" uses hahawakan (physically hold) for "handled" and kasanayan (skill/proficiency) for "practices" — pangangasiwaan and mga gawi/patakaran sa privacy are the idiomatic pair; "mga layuning operasyon" should be "mga layuning operasyonal". (3) Section headings are inconsistently handled — "Exam and badge" became "Pagsusulit at badge" but "Post-course survey" and "Test your knowledge" were left in English in the same file.
