examples.source: After completing the reading and activities in this course, click the button below to navigate to IBM Training
examples.translation: Pagkatapos mabasa ang mga aralin at gawain sa kursong ito, i-click ang button sa ibaba para pumunta sa IBM Training
examples.suggested: Pagkatapos matapos ang mga babasahin at gawain sa kursong ito, i-click ang button sa ibaba para pumunta sa IBM Training
examples.why: 'completing the reading and activities' becomes 'after reading the lessons and activities' — the completion requirement for the hands-on gawain is softened into mere reading, and 'aralin' (lesson) also replaces 'reading' (babasahin).

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Ito ay hahawakan nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.suggested: Pangangasiwaan ito nang naaayon sa mga gawi ng IBM sa privacy.
examples.why: 'hahawakan' is the physical sense of 'hold/handle' and 'kasanayan' means skill/proficiency, not customary practice; the ay-inversion adds stiffness a native legal-notice writer would avoid.

examples.source: ## Post-course survey / ## Test your knowledge
examples.translation: ## Post-course survey {#post-course-survey} / ## Test your knowledge {#test-your-knowledge}
examples.suggested: ## Survey pagkatapos ng kurso / ## Subukan ang iyong kaalaman
examples.why: These plain-English headings are left untranslated while the sibling heading 'Exam and badge' was rendered as 'Pagsusulit at badge' — an inconsistency within the same short file.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the Credly privacy notice tracks the English clause for clause (third-party processor, US location, name/email/badge shared, subsidiaries worldwide), and the audience framing ("dalawang magkaibang grupo... quantum computing ngunit wala sa HPC, at ... HPC ngunit wala sa quantum computing") preserves both directions correctly. Two things a native technical editor would still change: the section heading "Awarded Badge" is left in English while its sibling headings were translated ("Overview"→"Pangkalahatang-tanaw", "Exam"→"Pagsusulit"), an inconsistency within the same file; and "Ito ay hahawakan sa paraang naaayon sa mga kasanayan ng IBM sa privacy" calques "handled" with the physical-grip verb *hawakan*, where a Tagalog technical/legal writer would use "pangangasiwaan" or "pangangalagaan". Register is correctly informal — no po/opo — and domain terms kept in English (quantum computing, HPC, workflow, badge) are the conventional choice.

examples.source: ## Awarded Badge
examples.translation: ## Awarded Badge {#awarded-badge}
examples.suggested: ## Iginawad na Badge
examples.why: Left untranslated while the surrounding headings of equal rank were translated (Overview→Pangkalahatang-tanaw, Exam→Pagsusulit), so the heading set is inconsistent within the file. Not misleading, just an unfinished pass.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Ito ay hahawakan sa paraang naaayon sa mga kasanayan ng IBM sa privacy.
examples.suggested: Pangangasiwaan ito nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan ng IBM sa privacy.
examples.why: 'hahawakan' is the literal 'to hold/grip' sense of 'handle'; for data handling a native technical or legal writer uses 'pangangasiwaan'/'pangangalagaan'. Calque, meaning still recoverable.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the exam mechanics survive intact ("20 tanong… hindi bababa sa 16 para pumasa", "Kung hindi ka makakakuha ng pumapasang marka sa dalawang pagtatangka, pansamantalang mala-lock ang pagsusulit"), the maintenance caveat and the whole Credly/privacy paragraph are all present and faithful, and the informal register (kita/iyong, no po/opo) holds throughout. Two stylistic slips a native technical editor would still fix, both in the legal paragraph: "Ito ay hahawakan sa paraang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM" uses "hahawakan" (physically hold/grasp) for data handling where Tagalog policy prose says "pangangasiwaan"/"pakikitunguhan", and the stacked "ay"-passive reads as calqued English syntax. Also, "content offering" is flattened to plain "nilalaman", quietly dropping the "offering" sense — harmless to a learner but a lost qualifier.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Ito ay hahawakan sa paraang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.suggested: Pangangasiwaan ito nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.why: "Hahawakan" is the literal 'will be held/grasped' and is not how Tagalog privacy prose renders 'handled'; the "Ito ay …" passive also calques the English word order. Meaning is recoverable, so this is stylistic, not misleading.

examples.source: Your feedback will be used to enhance our content offering and user experience.
examples.translation: Ang iyong feedback ay gagamitin para mapahusay ang aming nilalaman at karanasan ng gumagamit.
examples.suggested: …para mapahusay ang aming mga inaalok na nilalaman at ang karanasan ng gumagamit.
examples.why: "Content offering" is reduced to bare "nilalaman", dropping the sense of an offering/catalog. A dropped qualifier only — nothing a learner would get wrong because of it.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the exam sequencing ("nilayong gawin pagkatapos basahin ang mga aralin"), the Credly consent chain (name/email/badge shared, notification email, global sharing with IBM subsidiaries and third parties) and both privacy-statement links all track the English exactly, and register stays casual (iyong/ka, no po/opo). The one thing a native technical editor would change is the calqued "Hahawakan ito sa paraang naaayon sa mga kagawian ng IBM sa privacy" for "It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices" — "hawakan" reads as physically holding; "Pangangasiwaan ito ayon sa mga kagawian ng IBM sa privacy" is the idiomatic rendering for handling personal data. Everything else (Pangkalahatang-tanaw, Badge na Iginawad, mga pangunahing kaalaman for "the essentials", quantum computing / badge / Credly left in English) is correct and consistent within the file.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Hahawakan ito sa paraang naaayon sa mga kagawian ng IBM sa privacy.
examples.suggested: Pangangasiwaan ito ayon sa mga kagawian ng IBM sa privacy.
examples.why: "Hahawakan" is a literal calque of "handled" and evokes physically holding something; for data/information handling a native writer uses "pangangasiwaan" (or "ituturing"). Meaning is not misleading, purely a fluency slip in the legal boilerplate.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination: the 2–3 hour estimate, the "maliban sa mga markado bilang opsyonal" caveat, the optional-links caveat, and all five course-outcome bullets track the English exactly, and the register stays casual (iyong/mo, no po/opo). The pre-course survey paragraph at line 15 is NOT a translator invention — it appears in 11–12 files in every locale subtree and pairs with the injected IBM survey note, so it is repo convention and not flagged. Two things a native technical editor would still change: "maaari kang sumunod sa link patungo sa IBM Training" calques "follow the link" — "sumunod sa" reads as obey/comply; Tagalog wants "sundan ang link" or "i-click ang link". And "basahin ang lahat ng teksto, maliban sa mga markado bilang opsyonal" uses "mga markado" as a bare noun, which is clipped; "maliban sa mga may markang opsyonal" is the natural phrasing. Both are stylistic, neither misleads.

examples.source: you can follow the link to IBM Training to take a badging exam if you wish
examples.translation: maaari kang sumunod sa link patungo sa IBM Training upang kumuha ng badging exam kung nais mo
examples.suggested: maaari mong sundan ang link papuntang IBM Training upang kumuha ng badging exam kung nais mo
examples.why: "sumunod sa link" is a direct calque of English "follow the link"; in Tagalog "sumunod sa" means to obey/comply with. A native writer uses "sundan ang link" or "i-click ang link".

examples.source: We recommend reading all text, not otherwise marked as optional, and watching all the videos.
examples.translation: Inirerekomenda naming basahin ang lahat ng teksto, maliban sa mga markado bilang opsyonal, at panoorin ang lahat ng video.
examples.suggested: Inirerekomenda naming basahin ang lahat ng teksto maliban sa mga may markang opsyonal, at panoorin ang lahat ng video.
examples.why: "mga markado" is used as a standalone noun ("the markeds"), which is stiff; the meaning survives but the phrasing is translationese rather than something a Tagalog technical writer would produce.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination anywhere: the exam facts survive intact (20 tanong / hindi bababa sa 16 para makapasa; "Kung hindi ka makakuha ng passing score sa dalawang pagtatangka, pansamantalang mala-lock ang pagsusulit" keeps the negative condition correct), and the Credly/privacy notice is complete with no dropped caveats. examples.source: Please take a moment to help us improve our course by filling out the following quick survey.

examples.why: "Ilaan ng sandali ang iyong oras" mis-assembles the actor/object focus — the imperative "ilaan" takes the thing allotted as its object, so this reads as "allot your time to a moment." A native writer says "Maglaan ka ng sandali." Meaning is still recoverable, so it is stiffness, not drift.

examples.source: Congratulations on completing this course!

examples.suggested: Binabati kita sa pagkumpleto ng kursong ito!
examples.why: The file's casual convention is fine, but clipped English "Congrats" is chattier than the surrounding prose and is not what a Tagalog technical writer would put at the head of a course-completion section; "Binabati kita" is informal and idiomatic without the slang drop.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Ito ay pamamahalaan nang naaayon sa mga patakaran ng IBM sa privacy.
examples.suggested: Pamamahalaan ito nang naaayon sa mga kagawian ng IBM sa privacy.
examples.why: "Practices" is rendered as "patakaran" (policies), a narrower legal category than the source's practices; in a privacy notice that distinction is deliberate. The "Ito ay ..." fronting is also a English-style calque where verb-initial "Pamamahalaan ito..." is the natural Tagalog order.

editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout this short overview page: "quantum processors having 100 or more qubits" is rendered exactly as "mga quantum processor na may 100 o higit pang qubits" with no quantity or hedge drift, "best practices" is consistently "pinakamahusay na mga gawi" in both the frontmatter description and the body, and the recommendation sentence keeps the casual register ("Para masulit ang kursong ito, inirerekomenda naming may kaalaman ka sa quantum information at quantum circuit") with no po/opo formality.

The technical body (overview paragraph, prerequisites) is faithful and reads naturally — "scaling", "quantum diagonalization", "matrix diagonalization" and "prerequisites" are sensibly kept in English and the informal register holds throughout (iyong/mo, no po/opo). The defects are all in the non-technical framing: the heading "Awarded Badge" is rendered "Napagtibay na Badge" ("ratified/confirmed"), where a native writer would write "Iginawad na Badge"; in the Credly notice "It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices" became "Ito ay pahahalagahan..." ("will be valued/esteemed"), which is not what "handled" means; "para tulungan sa pamamahala" is missing its actor/object ("para tumulong sa pamamahala"); and "Ang mga empleyado ng IBM ay maaaring tingnan ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement" mixes actor-topic with a patient-focus verb, a direct calque of the English clause ("Maaaring tingnan ng mga empleyado ng IBM ang..."). None of these teach a false quantum concept, so this is not a FAIL — but a native technical editor would change each one.

examples.source: ## Awarded Badge
examples.translation: ## Napagtibay na Badge
examples.suggested: ## Iginawad na Badge
examples.why: "Napagtibay" means ratified/confirmed/strengthened, not awarded. The badge is granted (igawad), not validated. Recognizable from context but plainly the wrong verb.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Ito ay pahahalagahan sa paraang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.suggested: Pangangasiwaan ito sa paraang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.why: "Pahahalagahan" = will be valued/held in esteem. The source is about how the data is handled/processed, a factual commitment, not an attitude toward it.

examples.source: ...a third-party data processor authorized by IBM and located in the United States, to assist in the administration of the IBM Digital Badge program.
examples.translation: ...para tulungan sa pamamahala ng IBM Digital Badge program.
examples.suggested: ...para tumulong sa pamamahala ng IBM Digital Badge program.
examples.why: "Tulungan" is transitive and here has no object — the sentence dangles. "Tumulong sa" is the form a native writer uses for "to assist in".

examples.source: IBM employees can view the IBM Internal Privacy Statement here.
examples.translation: Ang mga empleyado ng IBM ay maaaring tingnan ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement dito.
examples.suggested: Maaaring tingnan ng mga empleyado ng IBM ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement dito.
examples.why: Actor marked as topic (ang mga empleyado ... ay) with a patient-focus verb (tingnan) that already takes "ang IBM Internal Privacy Statement" — a calque of English SVO word order. The same pattern appears one sentence earlier ("Ang IBM Privacy Statement ay maaaring tingnan dito").

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination anywhere: the exam facts survive intact ("20 tanong", "hindi bababa sa 16 para makapasa", "Kung hindi ka makakakuha ng passing score sa dalawang pagsubok, pansamantalang mala-lock ang pagsusulit"), the survey/maintenance caveats are all present, and the casual register holds with no po/opo. examples.source: to assist in the administration of the IBM Digital Badge program
examples.translation: para tulungan sa pamamahala ng IBM Digital Badge program
examples.suggested: para tumulong sa pamamahala ng IBM Digital Badge program
examples.why: "tulungan" is the transitive/goal-focus form and demands a direct object (tulungan ang IBM); with none supplied the clause is grammatically incomplete. The actor-focus "tumulong" is what a native writer uses for "to assist in X".

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.

examples.why: "Hahawakan" is the physical sense of "hold/grip"; applied to personal data it is a calque of English "handled". Tagalog privacy/legal prose uses "pangangasiwaan" or "ituturing". Meaning is still recoverable, so this is stylistic, not misleading.

examples.source: IBM employees can view the IBM Internal Privacy Statement here.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads: the two prose paragraphs track the English exactly (immediate hands-on use of a quantum computer, no physics degree or years of programming needed, "Run" button kept verbatim), the informal register holds with no po/opo, and domain terms are sensibly kept in English (quantum computer, quantum computing, physics, programming, notebook). editor_note: No misleading content: the lesson numbering (2-6, 7-8, 9, 10, 11, 12-14), the "kung bago ka / kung mayroon kang malawak na karanasan" conditional pair, and the "maaaring bahagyang mag-iba" caveat all survive intact, and the register is consistently informal. What a native technical editor would change is phrasing: "at hand" is calqued literally as "na nasa kamay natin" (idiomatic Tagalog would be "na kasalukuyang tinatalakay natin"), "workflow" is over-translated to "daloy ng trabaho" while the file otherwise keeps English domain terms (circuit optimization, simulation, hardware), and "hosted externally" becomes the calque "naka-host nang panlabas sa GitHub". Two focus/particle slips read as MT rather than authored Tagalog: "**Mga Aralin 7-8** ay sinusuri ang quantum at classical na simulation" (patient-focus verb with an actor-topic; should be "Sinusuri ng mga Aralin 7-8 ang…") and "sumasaklaw tayo ng mga paksa" (sumaklaw takes sa, not ng). Separately, "good-faith estimates" is flattened to "mabuting pagtatantya" ("good estimates"), which shifts the honest-attempt hedge toward a quality claim — the following caveat clause keeps this from misleading, so it stays minor.
